result.summary: Read core-directives.md, docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md and decisions/0007-doors-time-in-t3h-reminder.md in full, then read every changed file (notification.ts, rateLimiter.ts, withdraw.ts's diff, event.ts, registration.ts, reminders.ts, reminderJobs.ts, reminder24h.ts, index.ts's diff, the three i18n files' diffs) line by line against the design. Every element matches design §1-§8 precisely: ComposedMessage's 'text'|'photo'|'skip' union, NotificationSender.sendPhoto, sendLedgeredNotification's extended step-5 table ('skip' -> skipped-stale with no sender call; 'text'/'photo' -> the matching sender method), rateLimiter's shared pacing/429/backoff table for both actions (InputFile wrapping for sendPhoto -- a genuine grammy requirement, not a deviation), findDoorsAgendaItem placed in event.ts per design's own reasoning, getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent/decideReconfirmOutcome/reconfirmRegistration mirroring decideWithdrawOutcome/withdrawRegistration's exact shape (reconfirmRegistration's UPDATE touches reconfirmedAt only), the two selectRegistrationsForReminder*'s window queries (evaluation-time-as-parameter, no now()), the two jobs' sequential (no Promise.all) processing, and index.ts's bot.init()-before-startScheduledJobs sequencing fix exactly as design §8 specifies. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC7 MYSELF with my OWN fixture (distinct chapter/venue/event/doors-item/times from BACKEND-DEV's -- chapter 'Reviewer Chapter' tz Europe/Moscow, event 'Reviewer Fixture Event A', doors at 2026-10-01T01:15:00Z, startsAt 2026-10-01T02:00:00Z): ran makeReminder3hJob against a live scratch Postgres, called buildEventCardContent (REQ-017's own renderer) on my own event fixture, and additionally computed the doors text a THIRD, fully independent way by calling formatDateTimeInTimezone myself with the same three arguments outside of both the job and the card renderer. All three values (my own independent computation, buildEventCardContent's agendaLines timeText, and the T-3h job's rendered caption) were asserted equal by strict `===`/`.includes()` on the literal string -- not 'looks similar'. PASS. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC8 MYSELF with my OWN fixture (event 'Reviewer Fixture Event B', agenda containing exactly two non-doors items: kind 'registration' at 01:40 and kind 'wrapup' at 04:45, deliberately different kind strings than BACKEND-DEV's own 'networking'/'close' fixture, to rule out the negative case being an artifact of one specific kind string): the T-3h caption contained catalog.reminder3h.startLabel's starts_at text, contained NO occurrence of catalog.reminder3h.doorsLabel, and contained neither non-doors item's own formatted time (both computed independently and confirmed to differ from startsAt's own text before asserting non-containment, ruling out a false pass from accidental time coincidence). PASS. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC3 MYSELF with a genuine two-OS-process test of my own construction (own fixture: chapter 'AC3 Chapter', event 'AC3 Event', registration + evaluationTime persisted to a sidecar file): process 1, a real separate `npx tsx` invocation, seeded the fixture, ran makeReminder24hJob(...).run(evaluationTime) to completion (real sender call + real ledger commit), appended exactly one line to a delivery-log file, then process.exit(0) -- no code runs after the send has durably resolved. Process 2, a WHOLLY SEPARATE `npx tsx` invocation opening its own fresh Pool/drizzle instance with no shared memory or module state with process 1, re-read the sidecar and re-ran the IDENTICAL job for the IDENTICAL evaluationTime: ledgerBefore=1, ledgerAfter=1 (unchanged), delivery-log line count before=1/after=1 (process 2 added zero lines). Exactly one message survived the two-process boundary, proving the DB-backed UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) constraint -- not any in-memory state -- is what enforces at-most-once here. All scratch files (scratch-ac3-p1.ts, scratch-ac3-p2.ts, sidecar, delivery-log) deleted after use; `git status --porcelain` confirmed clean. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC2 MYSELF with my own fixture: for the confirm ('I'll be there') path, called reconfirmRegistration directly and diffed EVERY column of the registrations row before vs. after via a raw SQL SELECT * (not just checking reconfirmed_at non-null) -- confirmed zero other columns changed (admission included), reconfirmed_at set non-null, outcome {kind:'reconfirmed'}. For the decline ('Can't make it') path, called withdrawRegistration directly (the same function reminder24h.ts's decline handler calls, per §7.2) on a separate registration and confirmed admission flips to 'withdrawn' via the real withdraw path, not a parallel implementation -- reminder24h.ts itself was independently re-read and contains no reimplementation of either decision table, only a call to reconfirmRegistration/withdrawRegistration plus i18n reply mapping. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC4 MYSELF with my own fixture: a registration withdrawn via withdrawRegistration BEFORE either job ran (real event 24h out, real withdraw call, then both makeReminder24hJob and makeReminder3hJob run for evaluation times inside their respective windows) -- zero notification_ledger rows of any kind for that registrationId, confirming selectRegistrationsFor...'s admission='admitted' filter excludes it from selection entirely for BOTH jobs, not just one. REQ-025 S9/S10 GUARANTEES RE-DERIVED AGAINST THE EXTENDED CODE: read notification.test.ts's diff in full -- every change is the pure `composeMessage: () => "text"` -> `composeMessage: () => ({kind:'text' as const, text: "text"})` wrapper-shape migration plus makeFakeSender gaining a sendPhoto stub; no assertion, fixture, or test body's logic changed. Ran the full suite myself (`TEST_DATABASE_URL=... npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism`, repo root): 22 files / 249 tests passed, 0 failed -- includes REQ-025's own S10 truth table (blocked-skips-both-classifications, marketing-broadcast-opt-in gate, transactional-bypasses-it), the concurrent-call race test, and the 429/backoff test, all still green against sendLedgeredNotification's now-extended step 5 and rateLimiter's now-generalized SendAction. The ledger-insert-then-send ordering (step 4 before step 5) is byte-for-byte unchanged in notification.ts's diff -- confirmed by direct read, not inference. No regression. withdraw.ts's composeMessage migration confirmed a PURE wrapper-shape change: diffed the closure's return -- the exact same newline-joined `[admittedPrefix, eventTitle, dateTimeText, qrLabel+qrToken, whatNext].join("\n")` string construction is unchanged; only the return is now wrapped `{kind:'text' as const, text}` instead of the bare string. sendPromotionNotification gained only an `export` keyword; no other line in the function changed. Confirmed by direct diff read, not by BACKEND-DEV's characterization. Domain logic outside handler bodies (decisions/0004): confirmed by direct read of reminder24h.ts and reminderJobs.ts. Both handlers in reminder24h.ts do pattern-match extraction, resolveActingUser, one domain-function call (reconfirmRegistration or withdrawRegistration), answerCallbackQuery, and an i18n reply switch on the returned outcome kind -- no decision logic is reimplemented in either handler body. reminderJobs.ts's composeReminder24h/composeReminder3h call domain reads (getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent, getEventByIdWithChapterTimezone, getVenueById, findDoorsAgendaItem) and assemble catalog strings/formatDateTimeInTimezone calls -- this is message composition (explicitly the design's own §5.1/§5.2 scope), not domain business-rule logic; the actual admission/eligibility rules live in domain/registration.ts and domain/reminders.ts, both grammy-free (grepped: no `from "grammy"` in either file). No `now()` in a time-dependent predicate (decisions/0006): both selectRegistrationsForReminder24h/3h take evaluationTime as an explicit parameter and never call SQL now()/current_timestamp; reconfirmRegistration's `at` parameter writes only reconfirmed_at (an audit/bookkeeping-style timestamp of when the action happened, same carve-out as withdrawRegistration's own `at`), never read back into a predicate. Confirmed by direct read of reminders.ts and registration.ts's diff -- no violation. Migrations reviewed as SQL directly (decisions/0005): confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat -- apps/bot/drizzle/` -- ZERO migration files touched by this diff. `git grep -n "doors_at|doorsAt"` across apps/bot returns exactly one hit, a comment in schema.ts explaining the column's deliberate absence -- independently confirms AC9 and the design's own 'Schema change: NO' header claim. No SECURITY-REVIEWER migration sign-off is triggered (S13 N/A -- no migration exists). Workspace/build-output check: `git diff master...HEAD --stat` touches only existing apps/bot/src files, docs/agents/design/, and this run's own handoffs -- no new npm workspace, no apps/* rename, no build-output directory moved. No scratch docker build required per this role's trigger condition. COMMANDS RE-RUN MYSELF, REAL OUTPUT (repo root; scratch Postgres bot-postgres-1 started and re-migrated by me via `npx drizzle-kit migrate`, confirming no new migration to apply): `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces clean (Next.js build succeeded; apps/bot's tsc clean). `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (apps/web: same 2 pre-existing unrelated LCP warnings as REQ-025's own review, unchanged by this diff; apps/bot: 0 problems). `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, full suite) -> 22 files / 249 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's reported count exactly, independently re-run by me. Scope check: diff touches exactly the design's own file list (notification.ts/.test.ts, rateLimiter.ts, withdraw.ts, event.ts/.test.ts, registration.ts/.db.test.ts, the two new reminders.ts/reminderJobs.ts(+.db.test.ts), the new reminder24h.ts/.test.ts, the three i18n files, index.ts) plus docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md and this run's own handoffs. No scope creep. All my own scratch verification files (apps/bot/scratch-verify-reviewer.ts, scratch-ac3-p1.ts, scratch-ac3-p2.ts, sidecar/delivery-log) were deleted immediately after use -- `git status --porcelain` confirmed clean before writing this handoff. MINOR issue carried forward from BACKEND-DEV's own handoff (runner.ts's internal-logger-vs-threaded-logLevel gap, now with real effect since REQ-026 ships real jobs): reviewed and AGREE this is correctly disclosed rather than silently fixed or silently ignored -- the design (§5, §8) does not name runner.ts as a file to change, so widening this run's scope to add a logger parameter would itself be out-of-scope creep. No rework needed; forwarding the finding unchanged.

issues.title: Carried forward unchanged from BACKEND-DEV's handoff: scheduler/runner.ts's internal-logger deviation now has real running effect
issues.description: REQ-025's step-02-backend-dev.json first disclosed that startScheduledJobs constructs its own internal createLogger('debug') rather than threading index.ts's configured logLevel, flagged as inert only while the job list was empty. REQ-026 ships two real 5-minute-interval jobs, so any job failure is now actually logged via runner.ts's own fixed-'debug' logger rather than index.ts's process-wide config.logLevel. Reviewed and agreed this is correctly out of this run's scope (design §5/§8 does not name runner.ts as a file to change) -- forwarding unchanged rather than either fixing it unrequested or silently dropping it.
issues.recommendation: Unchanged from BACKEND-DEV's own recommendation: a future requirement should add a logger parameter to startScheduledJobs if the configured logLevel needs to gate scheduled-job failure logs.

result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) -- mandatory, S9/S10 are extended here (sendPhoto path, buttons, the new reminder_24h/reminder_3h kinds, the reconfirm/decline callback handlers touching admission state and PII-adjacent QR tokens). My own assessment: the ledger-based idempotency mechanism, blocked/broadcast-opt-in gating, and admission-state writes are all unchanged in their guarantee-bearing logic and independently re-verified as extended correctly (AC2/AC3/AC4/AC7/AC8 own-fixture re-derivation above). SECURITY-REVIEWER should independently confirm rather than take this as sufficient, per this pipeline's re-derive rule -- with particular attention to the T-3h QR photo send path (a personal check-in credential now transiting the same rate-limited sender as marketing-adjacent text) and the reminder24h:confirm/decline callback_data pattern's registrationId exposure (same shape withdraw.ts's own pattern already uses, but worth confirming under S-series scrutiny specifically for this new surface).
